title: Dead vs living faith: believe God vs believe in God (Augustine)
source_text: IV. Itaque prior illa fides in multis impiis & hypocritis reperitur: posterior duntaxat in vere piis & bonis. Prior assensus est mere speculativus, qui in intellectu theoretico haeret. Posterior est assensus practicus, qui affectum movet, & voluntatem afficit. Quocirca prioris actum Scholae exprimunt per credere Deo, quod significat simpliciter Deo loquenti assentiri: posterioris per credere in Deum, quod cum assensu fiduciam in Deum, & Dei amorem includit; juxta illud Augustini, Quid est credere in Deum? credendo amare, credendo diligere, credendo in eum ire, & ejus membris incorporari: Proinde prior illa fides mortua & otiosa est. Sicut enim corpus sine Spiritu mortuum est, ita & fides sine operibus mortua est, ut testatur Jacobus epistolae cap. 2. altera vero viva est, & per charitatem operans, totamque quam Christus a nobis exigit, obedientiam secum trahit.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore that former faith is found in many impious and hypocrites; the latter only in the truly pious and good. The former assent is merely speculative, which sticks in the theoretical intellect. The latter is practical assent, which moves the affection and affects the will. Hence the Schools express the act of the former by believing God, which means simply assenting to God speaking; of the latter by believing in God, which with assent includes trust in God and love of God; according to that of Augustine, What is it to believe in God? by believing to love, by believing to cherish, by believing to go into him, and to be incorporated into his members. Accordingly that former faith is dead and idle. For as the body without the Spirit is dead, so also faith without works is dead, as James testifies in chapter 2 of his letter; but the other is living and working through charity, and draws with it the whole obedience Christ requires of us.
pass_b_english: Speculative assent ('believe God') is dead; practical trust-love ('believe in God') lives.
Augustine: believing in God is loving and joining his members; James: faith without works is dead.

choices.why: Includes trust and love, not bare assent.
